text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The energy monopoly in Viru county is breaking up as several large users are planning to build their own gas-fired power stations.

- Estonia's political situation is strangely right-wing, where proposed protective tariffs and progressive income tax have been described as a return to socialism, Foreign Minister Toomas Hendrik Ilves said at a conference on ideology.
- The Rural People's Party will not give up the idea of protective tariffs, faction chairman Tiit Tammsaar declared yesterday.
- Illegal residents refrain from registration as they fear repressions and see no use in signing up. Their number is estimated at 20,000 - 50,000.
- The 100 km/h top speed limit will fall to 90 on Saturday.
- Patrick Broe, owner of the US firm OmniTRAX and potential buyer of Estonian railway cargo traffic, called for the company's privatisation to be speeded up.
- Korea banned an Estonian animated cartoon film "1895" and three more cartoons, but has not explained the reasons why.
- The premier has demanded that all ministry chancellors and vice-chancellors resign from administrative boards of state-owned enterprises by September 1.
- The Russian firm Orenburgneft will not build an oil terminal in the Bekker Port in Tallinn because of a political row over the issue.
